standard_prerequisites: Context span 1103-1140: with R = k[y, z, a_1, a_2, ...]/(ya_i, a_i a_j) and f the residue class of z, the ring map R[[x]] -> R_f[[x]] is not flat - the kernels I of y : R[[x]] -> R[[x]] and J of y : R_f[[x]] -> R_f[[x]] satisfy J != I R_f[[x]], proved by comparing the coefficient of a_n after reduction mod (y, a_1, ...), Noetherian finiteness in k[z][[x]], and Algebra lemma-characterize-integral-element giving the absurd integrality of z^{-1}x; flatness would force J = I R_f[[x]] by tensoring 0 -> I -> R[[x]] -> R[[x]] -> 0
x-adic completion of power series rings: R[[x]] is x-adically complete, and localizing at a coefficient-ring element commutes with power series: R[[x]]_f = R_f[[x]]
core_obligations: Set A = R[[x]] with R from the context; A is complete with respect to the principal ideal I = (x)
The localization A_f equals R_f[[x]], and its x-adic completion is R_f[[x]] itself (already complete)
Hence A_f^ = R_f[[x]], and the context proves R_f[[x]] is not flat over R[[x]] = A
proof_roadmap: Instantiate A = R[[x]], I = (x) from the context ring
Identify A_f with R_f[[x]] and note x-adic completeness
Conclude non-flatness from the context computation
